feedback.details: Diagram passes mmdc validation (exit 0). All special characters are properly handled — no raw <, >, or & inside the diagram block. Node labels use \n for line breaks, which is correct Mermaid syntax. The diagram uses flowchart LR (the required format) and has a YAML frontmatter title. One minor observation: the edge labels use verbose phrases like 'Manually reads seed packet data' (line 45) without explicit directionality tags like [User -> System], which could be seen as a relationship specification gap rather than a syntax issue.

All six required entities are present in the diagram: User (line 37), Plant Tracking System (line 38), Hermes Agent/Telegram (line 39), Phomemo M120 Printer (line 40), Seed Packet Data Source (line 41), and Weather Service (line 42). Every node participates in at least one inbound or outbound edge — no orphan nodes. C4 quality note: Weather Service on line 42 is labeled '(External, Optional)' without a specific technology annotation (unlike Hermes which has '(Telegram, External)'), which is a Medium C4 quality issue per guidelines — every container should show a specific technology choice.

All three required sections are present: '1. Scope' (line 7), '2. Assumptions & Constraints' (line 10), '3. Component Definitions' (line 18). All six diagram components are defined in section 3 with PRD requirement ID mappings (lines 19-24). However, the PRD mappings are very broad ranges rather than precise one-to-one mappings. For example, 'Plant Tracking System' (line 20) maps to 'PRD FR6-FR40, FR46-FR50' — that's 48 requirement IDs lumped into one component definition, making traceability difficult to audit. 'Seed Packet Data Source' (line 23) maps only to 'PRD FR6' but this is described as 'manually read by the user' — which blurs the line between a component and a user activity.

All 10 diagram edges have typed labels with some interaction detail and directionality (lines 45-54). However, the labels lack the explicit directional format specified in the contract. For example, line 45 'Manually reads seed packet data' is a descriptive action but does not include '[User -> Seed Packet Data Source]'. The contract requires labels like 'QR Code Scan [User -> System]' or 'MQTT Telemetry [System -> Printer]' — the current labels are verbose phrases without explicit directionality markers. Line 51-52 use 'via HTTPS/REST' which specifies protocol, and line 53-54 use 'via Bluetooth' which is good. Line 49-50 use 'via Telegram' which is acceptable. But lines 45-48 (user-internal edges) are the weakest — they describe actions without protocol specification or directionality tags.

File fails markdownlint with 25+ errors. Specific issues: (1) MD025 at line 5: two top-level headings — YAML frontmatter title on line 2 and H1 on line 5 create 'single-title/single-h1' conflict; (2) MD022 at lines 7, 10, 18, 26, 31: headings are not surrounded by blank lines; (3) MD013 line-length violations at lines 8 (207 chars), 16 (145 chars), 19 (111 chars), 20 (150 chars), 21 (126 chars), 22 (115 chars), 23 (143 chars), 24 (122 chars), 27 (138 chars), 28 (182 chars), 29 (188 chars) — all exceed 80 character limit; (4) MD032 at lines 11, 19, 27: lists should be surrounded by blank lines; (5) MD031 at line 32: fenced code block not surrounded by blank lines; (6) MD047 at line 55: file should end with a single newline character. The file has not been fixed from Round 2's same critical failures.

Section 4 (line 26) documents all three required scenarios: (1) Network Partition (line 27): states it falls out of C1 scope and 'the system will queue operations locally and sync on reconnect' — but this conflicts with the 'falls out of C1 scope' claim since queuing is an implementation detail; (2) Hardware Failure — Phomemo Offline (line 28): states it falls out of C1 scope with 'No automatic queuing is implemented in MVP; user must reprint when printer is back online' — adequately addresses the scenario; (3) Data Latency/Consistency (line 29): states it falls 'in C1 scope (accepted as manual process)' with vague 'system ensures data integrity once entered'. All three cases are present but descriptions are brief. The Network Partition handling is particularly thin — it states a behavior (queue and sync) without explaining what operations are queued, for how long, or what happens if the queue fills. The consistency claim for data latency is handwavy — no specifics on what 'data integrity once entered' means.

overall_summary: The c1-context.md file has an architecturally sound C1 diagram that passes mmdc validation with all six required entities present and connected. The adversarial edge case section documents all three required scenarios with scope declarations. However, the file catastrophically fails markdownlint with 25+ errors (MD025, MD022, MD013, MD031, MD032, MD047) — this is a recurring critical issue from prior rounds that has not been remediated. The relationship specification lacks explicit directional markers like [User -> System] on many edges, and PRD traceability uses overly broad requirement ID ranges (e.g., FR6-FR40 for a single component) that make auditability difficult. The adversarial edge cases are present but shallow — particularly the network partition handling which states contradictory behavior (queuing operations) alongside an out-of-scope declaration.
